ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Within the width indicated by the dashed line, applying a uniform electric field of magnitude $E=2\mathrm{V}/\mathrm{m}$ directed vertically downward can deflect a certain positive ion with an initial velocity (horizontally to the right) of $\mathbf{v}_{0}=1\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ by an angle of $\theta=30^{\circ}$. The charge-to-mass ratio of this ion is $\frac{q}{m}=\sqrt{3} \times 10^{4}\mathrm{C/kg}$. Within the same width, if a uniform magnetic field directed perpendicularly out of the page is applied instead, keeping the initial velocity unchanged, the ion will pass through the region and also be deflected by an angle of $\theta=30^{\circ}$. The gravitational force on the ion is neglected.

1. What is the magnitude of the magnetic induction in a uniform magnetic field?
2. What are the times for ions to pass through the electric field and the magnetic field, respectively?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The left and right two vertical dashed lines in the figure indicate the width boundaries of the field region; a positively charged ion enters from the left with an initial velocity v0 horizontally to the right; vertical downward arrows are drawn in the field region, indicating that the electric field direction is downward; when the ion leaves the field region, its trajectory deflects downward, and the angle between the outgoing direction and the original horizontal line is labeled θ. Reasoning: Let the width between the two dashed lines be L. In the electric field, the positive ion is subjected to a force downward, and the acceleration is a=(q/m)E; the velocity in the horizontal direction remains vx=v0. When exiting, the deflection angle satisfies tanθ=vy/vx=(a tE)/v0, so tE=v0 tanθ/[(q/m)E], and L=v0 tE. Substituting E=2 V/m, v0=1 m/s, q/m=√3×10^4 C/kg, θ=30°: tE=tan30°/[2√3×10^4]=(1/√3)/(2√3×10^4)=1/(6×10^4)=1.67×10^-5 s. Therefore L=v0tE=1.67×10^-5 m. The magnetic field is perpendicular to the paper surface outward, and the positive ion's velocity is to the right; by the right-hand rule, the magnetic force is downward, and the trajectory is a circular arc. The radius r=mv0/(qB)=v0/[(q/m)B]. The outgoing tangent has turned through θ, and the horizontal displacement is L=r sinθ, therefore B=v0 sinθ/[(q/m)L]. Substituting L=1/(6×10^4) m, sin30°=1/2: B=(1×1/2)/[(√3×10^4)(1/(6×10^4))]=0.5/(√3/6)=√3 T. In the magnetic field the speed does not change, and the time to pass through the circular arc is tB=arc length/speed=rθ/v0. Also r=v0/[(q/m)B]=1/[(√3×10^4)(√3)]=1/(3×10^4) m, θ=30°=π/6 rad, so tB=(1/(3×10^4))(π/6)=π/180000=1.74×10^-5 s.
